reason: The native release job failed its unchanged 60 GiB free-space guard before downloading the successful package stage. The old inline cleanup neither reclaimed the documented Swift/GHCup installation directories nor reported the measured space.

actual_failure.stage: Reserve disk for image and native qualification
actual_failure.error: AssertionError: At least 60 GiB free disk is required
actual_failure.measurement_limit: The old guard did not log the actual available bytes. No exact shortage is inferred.

bounded_operational_recovery.request: One normal failed-job/dependants retry on a new hosted runner; successful package compilation is reused.
bounded_operational_recovery.observed: The unchanged disk guard passed and image/native assembly started. Full production qualification and immutable publication remain separate pending checks.

repair.cleanup_scope: Fixed unused SDK directories on disposable GitHub-hosted Linux only, including /usr/share/swift and /usr/local/.ghcup. No environment-supplied cleanup paths.
repair.protected_paths: Source, Go, Python, Node action runtimes, Docker, package artifacts and build caches are not cleanup targets.
repair.diagnostics: Whitelisted runner identity, actual free/used/total bytes before and after cleanup, fixed cleanup paths and pass/fail reason. No full environment or privileged work tree is collected.
repair.retention: One small JSON artifact per package/native job, uploaded even on preparation failure, expires after one day and is eligible for the existing two-hour completed-run cleanup.
repair.preflight: Reject omission of shared preparation, reduced disk budget, late preparation or missing failure diagnostics before expensive compilation.

cases: Original 60 GiB boundary and one byte below it
Cleanup errors fail without claiming space was reclaimed
Environment overrides cannot change fixed SDK cleanup targets
Every package/native workflow prepares disk before artifact download
Only completed known diagnostics enter bounded cleanup
Matching assessment hashes cannot waive disk preparation or failure reports

approval: A new source/workflow change needs actual independent human review on its final qualified head. The prior PR47 approval does not approve this repair.
traceability: Exact source, failure logs, successful same-source PR qualification, single retry intent/result and complete local validation are archived immutably before PR publication. Future hosted qualification, approval, protected merge and production publication are recorded separately.
